correctness.rationale: Use the published finite-graph cycle-mean theorem as a premise. The nine ordered color pairs satisfy an explicit exact edge-form coboundary identity, making CCA activity three times GHM activity for each coloring. Every simple cycle in the generalized theta graph joins two of the r paths, giving mean (t_i-t_j)/(ell_i+ell_j). Each fixed root color and residue-compatible increment vector has exactly the product of trinomial path counts; exactly three root colors occur. Equal-arm activity spectra follow from a multiple-of-three range and exact inclusion-exclusion. A lattice local central limit theorem, with variance 2/3 and span one, proves the stated sharp constant, and an endpoint-residue coupling proves the independent Gaussian limiting path sums. Independent exact coefficient and full functional-graph computations match on nine graphs for both CCA/GHM, totalling 318087 states per rule. The asymptotic follows from proof, not finite numerics. The scope has fixed r>=3 and all ell_i>=2; limit requires ell_i/n -> lambda_i in (0,infty).

The primary 2018 full text supplies the latter but does not give the residue-restricted trinomial population law or proportional-arm limit. The 1993 paper establishes foundational excitable models and discusses spatial asymptotics rather than the stated exact finite-network formula. Semantic searches returned nearby theta-graph square-coloring and geometric invariants, not the excitation-rate law. value.rationale: Generalized theta graphs are canonical minimal graphs with multiple independent overlapping cycles; their long-run excitation activity is governed by competing cycle means. The result supplies an explicit exact distribution over every initial state for arbitrary arm lengths and any fixed arm count, plus a sharp rare-synchronization exponent (r-1)/2 and geometric prefactor as the graph scales. The equal-arm count avoids state-space enumeration, while the Gaussian range law provides a natural graph-shape-sensitive limiting invariant. The result is more than a routine finite table or restatement of the known activity criterion and supplies a reusable finite-network benchmark.
